violations.description: Refrigerated Storage. — --Refrigerator or cold storage was insufficient or ineffective at maintaining potentially hazardous food at a temperature of 41F or less. Air temperatures of prep table with breakfast items and refrigerator near register were found at 50F. Food items also found above 41F in each unit. Refrigerated units should be capable of maintaining food temperatures of potentially hazardous foods at 41F or below.

Cleaning and maintenance of floors, walls and ceilings. — --Physical facilities (e.g. floors, walls, ceiling etc…) were not clean or not cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Wall behind the fryers was found dirty. This should be cleaned and maintained clean.

Food display and service. — --Potentially hazardous food was not kept at an internal temperature of 41F or below during display or service. Precooked hamburgers patties found at 48-50F in prep table. Potato salad found at 46F in refrigerator near register. Potentially hazardous foods should be maintained at 41F or below. **Items should be discarded.

Date marking and disposition of ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food. — --Refrigerated, ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food (prepared more than 24 hours ago) was not properly date marked. Multiple food items in the refrigerated pizza preparation cooler were found not marked with the date they were prepared. Potentially hazardous foods should be marked when held for greater than 24 hours so proper disposal can occur.

Sanitizing solution testing devices. — --Test strip or kit that accurately measures the sanitizing concentration was not provided. Testing strips were not available to check the sanitizing strength for the chlorine sanitizer used in the 3 compartment sink and the dish machine. Testing strips should be available and used to assure that the proper strength is used for sanitizing equipment.
